passages.title: Passage A: Memoized Once-Wrapper

items.stem: If fn() returns undefined on the first call, what happens on the second call?

options.A: fn runs again because cached is undefined
options.B: fn does not run again because called is already true

items.explanation: The separate boolean flag called prevents re-execution even when cached is undefined.

items.stem: What happens if makeOnce(fn) is called twice to create f1 and f2?

options.A: f1 and f2 share the same called flag
options.C: f1 and f2 each have independent called and cached bindings

items.explanation: Each invocation of makeOnce creates a fresh lexical environment.

part5.passage:
Fill in the exact JavaScript syntax:
1. To avoid loop callbacks sharing one index variable, declare the loop counter with [1] instead of var.
2. Inside a factory, a variable declared with [2] cannot be reassigned.
3. Calling fn.[3](ctx, argsArray) invokes fn with explicit this and an array of arguments.
4. An arrow function inherits [4] lexically from its enclosing scope.

items.explanation: let creates a block-scoped binding per iteration.
const prevents reassignment of the binding.
Function.prototype.apply takes (thisArg, argsArray).
Arrow functions capture this lexically.
out must be an Array ([]) so out.push works.
Using let gives each pushed arrow function its own i binding.
For n items indexed 0..n-1, the loop bound must be i < n.
Without return, buildFuncs(n) returns undefined.

part7.prompt:
Implement createCounter(start = 0, step = 1) using a closure. It must return an object with three methods:
- peek(): returns the current value without mutating it
- next(): advances the value by step and returns the NEW value
- reset(): resets the value back to start and returns start
Two counters created by createCounter must have completely independent state.

cases.name: default start and step
cases.expression: (() => { const c = createCounter(); return [c.peek(), c.next(), c.next()]; })()

cases.name: custom start and step
cases.expression: (() => { const c = createCounter(10, 5); return [c.peek(), c.next(), c.next()]; })()

cases.name: reset restores initial start
cases.expression: (() => { const c = createCounter(4, 2); c.next(); c.next(); return [c.reset(), c.peek(), c.next()]; })()

cases.name: independent closure instances
cases.expression: (() => { const a = createCounter(1, 1); const b = createCounter(100, 10); a.next(); b.next(); return [a.peek(), b.peek()]; })()

part7.explanation: Keep current in the closure scope of createCounter so each returned object maintains isolated private state.
